header.note: Source: strings.json. Target locale: French (fr). Microsoft Language Portal consulted for approved French gaming and UI terminology.

trans-unit.note:
CONTEXT: Full-screen overlay shown the instant the player clicks a mine and loses. Tone: Dramatic, punchy, exclamatory — mirrors the shock of the explosion. UI constraints: Short banner; prioritise impact over verbosity.
MICROSOFT TERMINOLOGY (via Microsoft Language Portal): - "Game Over" → approved French equivalent is "Partie terminee", used across Xbox, Windows, and MSN Games including Microsoft's own French Minesweeper localisation. "Fin de partie" also appears in Microsoft gaming contexts and is equally valid. - "BOOM" adapts to "BOUM" per French onomatopoeia conventions and Microsoft French localisation guidelines. "BOUM" is the standard French equivalent for an explosion sound. - French typography: a non-breaking space is required before "!" — ensure your CAT tool preserves this space in the final output.
TRANSLATION RATIONALE: "BOUM ! Partie terminee !" Uses Microsoft's approved gaming term; adapts onomatopoeia per French orthographic rules. Note: French does not use inverted punctuation (unlike Spanish).

CONTEXT: Full-screen overlay shown when the player successfully clears the board. Tone: Celebratory, triumphant. All-caps in the source to convey excitement. UI constraints: Short banner; mirror the energy and register of the English source.
MICROSOFT TERMINOLOGY (via Microsoft Language Portal): - "You Win" / "You Won" → approved French equivalent is "Vous avez gagne !" (present perfect, second-person plural/formal), used in MSN Games, the official French Minesweeper and Solitaire localisations, and Xbox achievement strings. - All-caps ("VOUS AVEZ GAGNE !") matches the source register and is consistent with Microsoft's French game UI string conventions. - Regional note: Canadian French (fr-CA) uses identical phrasing. For informal fr-CA, "T'AS GAGNE !" (colloquial Quebecois) is an alternative if the client specifies it. - French typography: non-breaking space before "!" required per orthographic convention.
TRANSLATION RATIONALE: "VOUS AVEZ GAGNE !" Matches Microsoft's approved French gaming terminology and preserves the all-caps register.
